description: On April 17, 2016, an active region on the sun's right side released a mid-level solar flare, captured here by NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory in stunning 4K ultra high definition. Solar flares are powerful bursts of radiation that can disturb GPS and communications signals.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: NASA's SDO Captures Stunning 4K Solar Flare

description: A new simulation brings scientists a step closer to understanding the kinds of light signals produced when two supermassive black holes, millions to billions of times the mass of the Sun, spiral toward a merger. This stunning visualization shows the dance of binary black holes and the warping of spacetime around them.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: Spiraling Supermassive Black Holes Simulation

description: On April 24, 2019, the Hubble Space Telescope celebrated its 29th year in orbit by premiering a never-before-seen view of the Southern Crab Nebula. This stunning cosmic hourglass of gas and dust is produced by the interaction between a red giant star and a white dwarf companion.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: Hubble's 29th Anniversary — Southern Crab Nebula

description: For the first time, scientists have ground and satellite views of STEVE (Strong Thermal Emission Velocity Enhancement), a mysterious atmospheric phenomenon that appears as a mauve-colored ribbon of light stretching across the sky. This video explores the science behind this stunning aurora-like display.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: The Aurora Named STEVE

description: NASA's flying telescope SOFIA captured a crisp infrared image of the center of our Milky Way galaxy. Spanning more than 600 light-years, this panorama reveals details within the dense swirls of gas and dust in high resolution, opening a new window into the heart of our galaxy.
subtitle: By NASA Ames Research Center
title: SOFIA Reveals New View of Milky Way's Center

description: The sun emitted a trio of mid-level solar flares on April 2-3, 2017. NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory, which watches the sun constantly, captured dramatic imagery of these events. Solar flares are powerful bursts of radiation that appear as bright flashes of light on the sun.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: April 2017 Solar Flare Trio

description: NASA revealed the first five full-color images and spectrographic data from the James Webb Space Telescope — the world's most powerful space telescope. These stunning images include the deepest infrared view of the universe ever taken, the Carina Nebula's cosmic cliffs, Stephan's Quintet, the Southern Ring Nebula, and an exoplanet atmosphere spectrum.
subtitle: By NASA
title: First Images from the James Webb Space Telescope

description: Building the James Webb Space Telescope is challenging. It is NASA's most ambitious and complex space science observatory. The mission required 10 new technologies to be invented, the dedication of hundreds of scientists and engineers, and decades of work. This video explores why Webb was worth the wait.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: James Webb Space Telescope: Worth the Wait

description: This narrated 12-minute video shows the James Webb Space Telescope's dramatic launch aboard an Ariane 5 rocket and its intricate deployment process — unfolding its sunshield, mirrors, and instruments as it journeyed to its orbit at the second Lagrange point, 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: Webb Telescope Launch and Deployment

description: NASA scientists explain the first full-color images and data from the James Webb Space Telescope in detail. From the deepest infrared image of the universe to the atmospheric composition of a distant exoplanet, experts walk through each groundbreaking observation and what it means for our understanding of the cosmos.
subtitle: By NASA Goddard Space Flight Center
title: Webb's First Full-Color Images Explained
